title: 1,257 event cards, 281 chains, one LLM: what worked and what it couldn't do
author: zenist69
selftext:
Built a Reigns-like about running a dying space station. Every number below came out of an LLM workflow, so here's the honest breakdown.



What worked:

\- Batching by category (energy, medicine, politics) instead of one giant prompt. Consistency held across 1,257 cards.

\- A fixed schema per card: title, scene, two choices, each with a one-line consequence note. The model fills slots instead of writing prose.

\- Generating the 281 chained follow-ups by feeding it the parent card and asking "what does this cause one cycle later".



What didn't:

\- It cannot balance numbers. Every fx value had to be hand-tuned.

\- Tone drifts after \~200 cards. Had to keep re-seeding style examples.

\- Chains that reference state (a dead character) need manual bookkeeping. The model forgets.



Human work was structure and editing, not writing.



Happy to share the schema or answer anything about the pipeline.

comments.author: No-Pollution7797
comments.body:
The dead character problem is the one I'd take away from the model entirely. Give each card a small requires/sets pair (requires: engineer\_alive, sets: engineer\_dead) and let the game filter the deck at draw time, so the model only has to fill in those two fields when it writes a card and never has to remember who died.



I'd also have it write one line of assumptions per card while generating, something like "assumes the doctor is still aboard", and turn those into requires tags during editing. That pass is where the chains that quietly bring someone back tend to show up. I work on a text game where an AI writes the story and it's the same rule there, anything that has to stay true lives in saved state, not in what the model remembers.

replies.author: zenist69
replies.body: Honestly, I haven't done any state validation. I played a few runs and nothing broke, which at 1,257 cards probably means I haven't hit the cases yet. So it's a gap, not a solved problem — your point stands.

replies.author: No-Pollution7797
replies.body: Fair, at that size a few runs mostly walk the common paths. A cheap first check would be a script that follows each chain and flags any card naming someone an earlier card already killed off.

replies.author: zenist69
replies.body:
Ran it. Full version: 1,258 cards, 361 chain edges — zero dangling references, zero unreachable cards. Only hits were in the 7-cycle demo: 14 chain hooks pointing at cards I'd stripped out to keep the demo small. Nothing player-visible.

Your point stands though — the check was cheap and should have existed from day one. Appreciate you taking the time to spell it out. Thumbs up.
